9.7.7. qnav.measurement.clock

9.7.7.1. clock.py

summary:

Contains the virtual clock/timer classes for estimating elapsed time. This module contains virtual clock classes that can be used for simulating recorded time (with errors and drift) within a simulated environment. This is namely to simulate clock errors within simulations.

authors:
Prof. Jason Ralph - jfralph@liverpool.ac.uk
Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk
version:

1.0.0 - First full implementation of module.

class qnav.measurement.clock.Clock(clock_bias: float = 0, bias_drift_rate: float = 0, start_time: float = 0.0, rand_seed: int = None)[source]

Provides the functionality of a system clock in a simulated environment. Distinct from typical sensor hardware, the clock represents a virtual clock that simulated the recording of elapsed time with configured error drift.

update(time_sec: float)[source]

Called every iteration to update clock measurement errors. As clock errors propagate with time, it is important that this method is called prior to every measurement update.

Parameters:

time_sec (float) – The current simulation time in seconds.

get_time(current_time: float) → float[source]

Returns the believed elapsed time since the start of the simulation. This is given in seconds (with considerations for rounding errors).

Parameters:

current_time (float) – The true current time of the simulation.

Returns:

The current time with clock errors applied (in seconds).

Return type:

float
